summary: Texas Forest Service tower in Panola County, about 140 ft tall in 1958; a 1993 sale notice offered it for dismantling and removal; FFLA lists two Beckville points as gone, neither tied to this tower.

facts.design: Four-legged tower with a grey, glass-enclosed cab
facts.status_note: FFLA list marks both Beckville entries (Loc 1 and Loc 2) gone, but no source read ties either point to this tower; a 1993 notice offered the tower for sale, dismantling and removal, and no source records when it came down

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey station description, dated 1958, describes the glass-enclosed cab tower with overall height about 140 feet
Notice dated January 15, 1993 invited sealed bids for the sale, dismantling and removal of Texas Forest Service towers, including the Beckville Fire Lookout Tower, Panola County

notes_for_editor: No build date, staffing history or fire record for this tower in the sources read; one search found none. The 1993 notice is an offer of sale, not a record of removal, so the gone status rests on the FFLA list. Height 42.7 m is converted from 'approximately 140 feet' on the 1958 NGS description. The NGS point is about 3.5 miles airline north of Beckville; compare it with the FFLA coordinates before publishing, since the sources do not state the town's own coordinates. The FFLA list also carries a second Beckville entry, Loc 2 at 32.29934, -94.43776, also marked Tower Gone (quoted in evidence). The story says neither FFLA point is tied to this tower, because no source read gives either point's location against the 1958 description or links the two entries to the tower; the gone status therefore rests on the name match. Compare both points with the NGS location before any stronger link is made. No access or site-condition source was found, so access is left out of facts.
